# Welcome {.unnumbered}

![](images/head.png){fig-alt="Simulation of Pleiotropic, Linked and Epistatic Phenotypes" width=62% .cover-banner}

::: {.book-intro}
Build simulations whose assumptions, genetic mechanisms, and realized outcomes
you can explain and check.
:::

We regard [AlphaSimR](https://gaynorr.github.io/AlphaSimR/) as the gold standard
for breeding-program simulation. simplePHENOTYPES is not intended to compete
with it. It is another tool for making simulation more widely used: bringing
your own data, exploring how genetic assumptions affect outcomes, and using
those results to understand a problem and make better decisions.

This book is for researchers in plant, animal, and human genetics with basic R
knowledge. Examples follow the tidyverse style, introduce unfamiliar functions,
and compare design parameters with simulated results in simple tables. It connects the
simplePHENOTYPES interface to the statistical models and computational methods
behind it. Worked examples come first; interpretation, assumptions, and theory
follow. Longer derivations belong in the appendices.

::: {.callout-note title="Working draft"}
Every chapter in the [chapter plan](development.qmd#sec-chapter-plan) now has a
worked draft, and every exported function and registered method has at least one
executed example. The pilot chapters passed independent scientific review. The
methods chapters passed a same-model theory review, with every error it found
corrected, and still await the independent cross-model review.
Example execution and scientific review are separate checks; the
[evidence register](equation-index.qmd#sec-evidence) records the status of each claim.
:::

## Start with a complete simulation

[A first simulation](first-simulation.qmd) starts with importing your own genotype
data and uses bundled observed maize genotypes for a reproducible walkthrough of
model specification, diagnostics, and file export. It also explains
why the requested variance allocation and the realized variance ratio can differ.

The book serves plant, animal, and human genetics with observed genotype
datasets from each context: the bundled maize panel, the HapMap Phase II subset
distributed with SNPRelate for [binary phenotypes](binary.qmd), and the
heterogeneous-stock mice distributed with BGLR for
[relationship matrices and prediction](prediction.qmd). The
[genotype input chapter](input.qmd) shows how each dataset is prepared.

## Three ways to read

- **Learn a workflow:** follow the worked chapters in order.
- **Find a function:** use the [public function index](functions.qmd).
- **Inspect a method:** follow the [implementation overview](architecture.qmd),
  [developer index](developer-index.qmd), and [equation index](equation-index.qmd).

## Version and scope

The examples are rendered against the package source in the same checkout as the
book. The source revision and package version are recorded in the
[build record](development.qmd#sec-build-record).

The book covers the modern API and keeps a dedicated chapter for the
frozen `create_phenotypes()` interface ([legacy interface](legacy.qmd)). The original package publication is
[Fernandes and Lipka (2020)](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12859-020-03804-y);
the current development interface includes methods added after that publication.
